<reason>A won by imposing a cleaner decision rule: both policies require consent, risk, and partnership review, so CON cannot treat that review as uniquely fatal, while CON never justified leftover permission barriers on safe outputs after real needs are protected. B’s translation and formation arguments were sharp but too narrow for the motion, collapsing partner preference into necessity and under-answering residual reuse.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Rebuttal 2: commercial reuse is in the default, but sequenced, documented exceptions protect genuine exclusivity without letting partner preference veto every output—leaving B’s inversion claim weaker than the residual-rights gap.</best_rebuttal>
